utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think the Prosecution has something to inform us before we have the witness. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. And I didn't want to take up much time today, but I did want to tell you that earlier this week investigators from the OTP in Bratunac interviewed two different witnesses that have provided some information that I think would significantly assist the Court. And I would like -- that we will be filing a motion to add them to the witness list. So I just wanted to alert you to that, and we are not laying out everything that they said. But basically we have a person that was a driver for Mr. Blagojevic that can help locate him around the brigade headquarters at certain times. And there is a truck driver that was involved in the burial of bodies from Kravica, not the reburial, but the actual burial at the key times and has some important information. Now, I don't think either of them have passports, so I don't think we're going to be able to get them here by February 6th, and I really don't want to have to schedule them in between this important time that I know we've all been looking forward to having -- get other work done and perhaps some rest. We were thinking that perhaps we could come to some agreement that at the Prosecution's rebuttal case that we be allowed to reopen our case just for these two short witnesses. And who knows, perhaps at that stage of the case, the issues that they resolve will -- or help revolve, I should say, won't be issues anymore. But we're also trying to get them for next week, but we are on schedule. And as you know, we only have four days next week. And it looks like we may be taking most of those days with the two witnesses who are scheduled. So we will be providing this in a written format. And for everyone's consideration. I have mentioned it briefly to Defence counsel, but I wouldn't bring this up if I didn't think it was important and it would help you. I told myself if we didn't finish by February 6th, I would jump off the balcony, so I really want to finish by that time. But these are people we just interviewed and now it's -- in a perfect world we would have interviewed them before. But we've now managed to find them with great cooperation from the local RS authorities, I should say. And we will be putting this down on paper because it's, I think, an important issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any brief, very brief, response from Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, if I may. First, I would object to these people coming in at the rebuttal stage. Secondly, I do agree with Mr. McCloskey that they may be important witnesses. Mr. Blagojevic as well as his Defence team has maintained throughout that we want all of the facts and all of the truth to come out before this Trial Chamber. So obviously, it is in our best interest as well that these individuals come and testify. I would prefer to have them testify before the Prosecution rests its case. I think that that would be the most appropriate way of doing it. We could take a recess and during that recess, for instance, we would be responsible for preparing a motion for judgement of acquittal, then bring these two witnesses in and then perhaps be given some additional time, a few days extra, perhaps a week, to complete a motion for judgement of acquittal. So we -- I think we can be -- we can work around this. But I would prefer the Prosecution to have every opportunity to put its case in one piece, because I think when we hear it all, I will be able to demonstrate that they have failed to meet their burden, at least at this stage with respect to large portions of the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, any response?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, prior to the beginning of this session, we were informed that these witnesses are connected with the Bratunac Brigade. And the Prosecutor told us that these two witnesses, practically speaking, had nothing to do with our client. So -- but for professional reasons, I join in this with my colleague, Mr. Karnavas. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blagojevic. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] I should like to state three very brief elements before this Chamber. First of all, I'm not satisfied with the quality of the cross-examination of the witness listed under the pseudonym P-130. Second, yesterday in the organisation of the Registry a meeting was held with myself here at the Tribunal, and at one point a representative of my imposed Defence appeared, an individual whom I fired a long time ago and whose work I still do not accept. In the meantime, he has availed himself of an opportunity to warn me and perhaps even threaten me with an agreement - at least that's how it was translated to me - that he has with the Tribunal, according to which he can do as he pleases. So practically speaking, he told me there was nothing I could do about it. All the time he was being very ironical, he laughed, and he almost said it would be better for you to keep your mouth shut and let me do as I please. Once again, I do not agree with him. I am against this person, and this is the only opportunity that I have to state this before this Tribunal. I should like to appeal to the Chamber to put an end to this engagement, the engagement of Mr. Karnavas, as soon as possible. Third, I also object to the decision of the Chamber, whereby it was allowed for the statement for the person by the name of Erdemovic to be admitted without his appearance before the Tribunal to testify in this case and to be subjected to the cross-examination, but not in the manner that this individual is conducting this cross-examination, in a most amateurish and perfunctory way. Thank you very much, Your Honours. This is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Blagojevic. According to the Rules of this Tribunal, this Bench believes that the communications between you and your counsel should enjoy some privileged rights, which mean that we, as Judges in this Bench, could not ask you or your counsel the contents, the contents, of your conversation. But anyway, we believe that we should encourage the contact between you and your counsel. As for the decisions, frankly speaking, Mr. Blagojevic, as I told you before, there was a decision rendered by the Appeals Chamber. And we are not entirely happy about certain paragraphs of this decision neither, but according to the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, we have to abide by whatever decisions rendered by the Appeals Chamber. So we regard this matter as over. As for the cross-examination of Mr. Erdemovic, I think it's just a technical issue, and your counsel, Mr. Karnavas and his team, could explain to you about our decisions. We cannot revisit this decision at this stage, unless you have an extraordinary reason to believe that your interest is going to be jeopardised by our decision. You could seek other remedies, like the appeals. But this Trial Chamber will be in a position to review your appeal to the Appeals Chamber to see whether there is an extraordinary reason to appeal. I think that's all I could say to you, Mr. Blagojevic. Yes. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just to confirm you understand me and so that I understand what you have just told me. I do not have anything against the decisions rendered by this Trial Chamber and by the Appeals Chamber. I am not satisfied with the situation I have found myself in. Nothing has been changed. The situation has exacerbated in a most progressive manor, and things are only likely to get worse. This is perfectly clear. That's one thing. Second, I do not have any legal assistance. I do not have any reliable information. I am not receiving any reliable and good-quality, well-intentioned information. Everything that's happening here is blurred, as far as I'm concerned, and I'm being skeptical about everything. I simply do not have anyone to address my complaints to. I do not have anyone I can trust in terms of having reliable and the best quality information that can be obtained. This is what I don't have at this moment, and this is what is making my situation very difficult. There is no contact, there is no communication whatsoever between myself and Karnavas. I do not trust Karnavas at all. Perhaps I do not fully understand the issue of the 92 bis statement. I do not understand it because it's a legal issue, after all. But I can see that through the Witness P-130, the situation is being -- is getting more complicated because of this issue. And there is no need for that. This is all interconnected. One cannot have one thing without the other. Everything is very important, very significant. Once again, everything is interconnected because it has bearing on what is being at issue here on the examination in general. That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the transcript has registered your statement correctly there. At this moment, I have no more comments on this very issue. Another issue is about the two witnesses that are going to be called. We believe that we would like to hear those two witnesses in the Prosecution's case, if possible. We might have a short break, as the Defence counsel suggested, and then we'll arrange a hearing, maybe for two or three days, maybe even less, to finish these witnesses so that the Defence could be in a better position to prepare their case. I hope the Prosecution could do whatever possible to make it, and don't jump over the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Mr. Karnavas, for your flexibility. We are trying to do just that and to try to get these folks here as soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Another matter is concerning of the translation issues raised by the Defence counsel concerning Milosevic's case. I have received some correction notes from the translation booth. They make -- they made some corrections concerning the Milosevic's transcript, which can be found on the page 29682, line 19 to 20. Before the correction, the question put to Mr. Deronjic is: "You say that Vidoje Blagojevic, commander of the Bratunac Brigade, ordered you to go to Srebrenica, this is in paragraph 184 on the 11th of July?" The answer is: "Yes." After the correction and checking with the transcript, now we got I believe the correct version. That is: "Q. On the 11th of July - and you say this in paragraph 184 - Vidoje Blagojevic, commander of the Bratunac Brigade, told you that there was an order to go to Srebrenica. This is what you said, is it not?" The answer is: "Yes, that's correct." Well, there is some differences there, and with the legal implications, I believe the parties will get it. Another matter is about the 92 bis documents concerning with Stephanie Frease. The Trial Chamber checked with all the entries in this bundle of the documents. We believe there's no problem with the authenticity and integrity of those intercept-related materials. So we believe that we are in the position to make an oral ruling to admit them into the evidence. Of course the counsel for Mr. Jokic will have the full right to call this witness in the future in their case if they find that there is some very special matters which directly related to the acts and conducts of his client. The Trial Chamber will do its best, as we did with the Prosecution, to help the Defence to get the witness to testify in their case. It is so decided. Well, having said that, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry for having kept you waiting outside for a long time. Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, could we go to private session for this series of questions? Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember, you said that the transportation of the from the Bratunac area was completed in the night between the 13th and the 14th. Where did you spend the rest of that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the rest of that night on the clearing or the plateau in front of the gym of the Orahovac elementary school. If you look from the top part, I was in the bottom corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean to say that you were out in the open, that you didn't sleep anywhere, but that you spent the night in the vicinity of the school and the gym out in the open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I slept out in the open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether that evening in the gym of the elementary school, whether there were any lights on, whether the power was on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Jasikovac did check the area, and he entered the gym on two or three occasions on the 14th; that was on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally notice any lights being on or the lights being off since you spent the rest of the night in the open next to the gym and next to the school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice and I did not enter the gym at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have noticed if the lights had been on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 14th of July in the morning, you went to the Zvornik Brigade command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure and will you confirm today under oath that you were not present during the morning roll call in the Zvornik Brigade command on the 14th of the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question, but please go slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: Are you sure that you were not on the 14th, in the morning, the 14th of July, present at the morning roll call of the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of July in the morning, I was in front of the gym of the Orahovac elementary school. I was not present at the roll call of the Zvornik Brigade -- at the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at all go down to the Zvornik Brigade command to do anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire course of the operation in Orahovac from my arrival until its completion, until the completion of the execution operation in Orahovac, I never once left Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that whether any meeting of the security officers of the Drina Corps and the Zvornik Brigade was held in the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We understand that that's what you're saying, but the question is: Did you have any knowledge of the meeting of the officers that was held that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any knowledge. I didn't know about that meeting at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at a later date hear about this meeting being held in the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me anything about it, and I didn't have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Drago Nikolic tell you later on about any kind of a coordination meeting or any other kind of meeting that was held in the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic didn't tell me anything about any meetings. He just told me that he had some duties to take care of and that he was unable to come to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. He spoke about the duties he had in the afternoon hours. Did he tell you anything about the duties that he had in the morning of the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have any contacts with Drago Nikolic throughout that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that the first time that you saw him on that day of the 14th was in the early evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps this would be a good time for you to tell us more specifically at what time in the early evening. What could have been the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be specific, but it was after 5.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So until that time, until Drago Nikolic came and told you what you have already told us, no executions had been carried out and the executions had not begun by that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of the two persons that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher to help me present the witness the Defence exhibit marked for identification purposes as D66. Again, it's part of the transcript from the trial containing the testimony of witness Mevludin Oric. This is the testimony of Oric, Mevludin. The date is the 21st of July, 2003, page 1.357 of the transcript, lines 15, 16, 17, and 18. I would now like the witness to have a look at this, too, both the English and the B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, one of the survivors of the events in Orahovac testified before this Tribunal and before the Trial Chamber. When asked by the Prosecutor the following questions: "Do you know roughly what time of day it was that your group was executed?" And the witness answered: "I think it was about 1.00 or 2.00. I did not have a watch, so I can't say accurately what the time was. But I think it was about that time, because the sun was high up -- well high up. I think it was in the afternoon." Yet, you testify here today that there had been no executions, least of all organised executions, until the evening, the early evening, until the arrival of Drago Nikolic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said with the exception of the two persons that were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you say, but I said "no organised executions," because this we cannot label as an organised execution. So do you still maintain that during the day of the 14th of July until the early evening no -- no one was taken out of the gym and that no organised executions had taken place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to say that the testimony of Mevludin Oric before this Tribunal, in which he stated that these events took place between 1.00 and 2.00, that it simply does not correspond with the actual chronology of the events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to comment on the testimony of Mr. Oric. I can only comment on my own testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still, even after being confronted with the testimony of this witness given before this Tribunal, still maintain that on the 14th of July, there had been no organised executions until the early evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now embark upon a different line of questioning, and I will, at any rate, leave it to the Trial Chamber to give appropriate weight to the testimony of both witnesses, the one present here and the one from another trial. Could you please clarify for us this conversation that you had with the duty officer in the Zvornik Brigade on the 14th of July. Could you please tell us more precisely when that took place, what time of day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be specific about the time of day, but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be closer to noon or closer to the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my estimate, it would have been sometime between 1.00 and 3.00, or maybe 4.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to remind you of the part of your statement given to the investigators on the 19th of August, 2002. You mentioned this conversation, and you said that you did not remember who the duty officer was, but that you were reminded by the investigator when he mentioned the name. On that occasion you said that the contents, as far as you could remember, of the conversation between you and the duty officer was as follows: When you were asked what the duty officer told you, you stated that the duty officer informed you as follows: "I don't know anything. If I can find somebody, I will send people up there to you." Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke with the duty officer, Major Jokic, who was there at the time, I was reminded of that fact by the investigator who was -- investigators who assisted my in this respect. I first asked him whether he knew whether Drago was, because I needed to talk to Drago Nikolic, the security chief, because I had problems, and whether he could organise some personnel to be sent to me to assist me, as assistance was needed in that location. He told me that he didn't have enough men, but that he would try to do as much as he could. After a certain period of time - and I cannot be specific about how long that was - the group that I mentioned arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately after this conversation, you, as you testified here today, here, phoned Lazar Ristic, the deputy commander of the 4th Battalion, asking him to send some men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you call Lazar Ristic because you concluded on the basis of your conversation with the duty officer that perhaps there wouldn't -- there aren't men available to help you guard the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called him because I thought that even if the first group arrived, it wouldn't be amiss for the second group to arrive also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not receive any promises that the people from the Zvornik Brigade would come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty operations officer, Jokic, didn't tell me that I would get men. Lazar Ristic, likewise, didn't tell me that he would send men, but they said that they would do as much as they could and that if they found somebody, they would send them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at first you didn't know who the duty officer was at the beginning of your interview with the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I didn't know; I said that I couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it that reminded you that it could be Dragan Jokic after seven years have passed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well when the two of us spoke, when they mentioned the name, the very name reminded me of the conversation, because I was in Orahovac where men who were about to be executed were located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is precisely why I want to ask you this question. Is there any document or any piece of evidence that reminded you of the fact that you spoke to the duty officer by the name of Jokic, that that was the name of the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no document there at the time to serve as a reminder, but the very book of the duty officer, when I had the opportunity to look at it, made me realise that my recollection was accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this group that arrived in Orahovac, you say that even Sreten Milosevic was with them too. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he told you that he himself would organise the group to guard the prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say that he would organise the group to guard the prisoners. He took part in organising the overall security when he arrived, and that included this group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that Sreten Milosevic organised the guarding of the prisoners, not only with the group that arrived with him but with all the others who were present there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He joined those who were already present there. He helped me and all the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that at that time Sreten Milosevic was also in the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was in the Zvornik Brigade command or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where had he come from to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had come from the Zvornik Brigade, but I don't know exactly from where, and he came when he was asked to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this conversation that you had with the duty officer over the insecure line, you didn't tell him anything about the fate of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you had told him that the guard of the prisoners of war should be redoubled. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite specific, I told him that if he had the capability, that he should send a group to help us because such assistance was necessary to provide security for the prisoners held in the gym of the elementary school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We heard an expert testimony by Mr. Richard Butler, a military expert, who said that prisoners of war are a legitimate and legal consequence of combat operations. We also heard your testimony, where you said that you did not know what the fate of the prisoners would be until the arrival of Drago Nikolic, but that you had assumed what could possibly be their fate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that guarding prisoners of war is a legal and legitimate military task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am not familiar with the law in this -- to such an extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, to the extent you are familiar with it, would you agree that prisoners of war, generally speaking, must be guarded, that there can be -- there cannot be any prisoners of war who are not guarded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I haven't studied these issues, and I cannot possibly talk about the regulations and obligations on the basis of such law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to ask you: Do you know who Tanic Tanacko is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to refresh your memory. He was the finest officer of the Zvornik Brigade, otherwise an economist by profession. Do you remember him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who I'm talking about when I say Tanac Tanacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you know if he was with the group of people who arrived with Sreten Milosevic in the afternoon of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot -- I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that he was there but that you did not see him or you do not remember him being there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the assistance of the usher at this point, Your Honour, so that we could show the witness the statement which this individual gave to the investigators of the OTP. The statement in question was given by Tanac Tanacko. We will show the witness the B/C/S version and the English translation of the interview, which was conducted with this individual who declared in this interview that he did indeed arrive in Orahovac at one point and that he was brought -- he had been brought from the rear of the Zvornik Brigade to Orahovac to perform guard duty of the detainees. I will be referring to page 18, line 3 from the bottom in the English version, and page 19 up to the line 14 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the relevant passage in the B/C/S version is on page 17 in the middle of the page. For practical purposes, let us just read the relevant portion. So we are talking about the witness who was with the group that arrived in Orahovac and who is telling how it came about that they arrived in Orahovac. He says that on that day they had set out from Standard in a small truck, that there was a shift change, and asked by the Prosecutor who told you to get on to the truck, he said: "Miladin Mijatovic. He was the one who saw me in the corridor." The investigator goes on to ask: "Who is Miladin Mijatovic?" And the witness replies: "I don't know. For a while in 1992 he was the commander of the battalion. Later, he was the chief purveyor of fuel and other supplies for the army." The investigator then asks: "In July of 1995, what was his position?" The witness replies: "I don't know. He was there with the brigade command, but I don't know what he was. He wore civilian clothes and he came to the command all the time." And he finishes by saying: "He was on very good terms with the commander." The question: "Who was the commander at the time? The witness replies: "Pandurevic. Whether he was the commander or not, I don't know, but I know that he was a very good friend of his." Have you been able to read this portion of the statement of Tanac Tanacko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So one of the individuals who arrived in this group says that he had been sent from the rear, the rear in this case being the finance department, by Miladin Mijatovic. Miladin Mijatovic told him to go there. Do you know who Miladin Mijatovic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber who this person is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a reserve officer, a member of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What particular function did he perform at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the logistics department, in the rear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the duty or the function of Sreten Milosevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the deputy commander for logistics at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, the Zvornik Brigade of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was Milenko Jovanovic, whom you remembered having arrived with this group as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Jovanovic was the headquarters' commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a duty officer issue orders to the deputy commander for logistics, or is it the case that he can only convey to him what is being requested of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of your questions would require me to examine the relevant regulations and statutory provisions regarding the appointments within the Zvornik Brigade. I don't know how the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade were organised in terms of sending these people to various assignments, because I no longer had any contact with anyone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that for all practical purposes you do not know whether the duty officer with whom you had talked conveyed this message to anyone else, because you were not present there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to whom he conveyed this message and who finally acted on it. I just know that I talked to the duty operations officer, who at the time was Miodrag Jokic [as interpreted] with the request for assistance in terms of personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we have investigated this case and we would like to have you confirm what you have just said. On that occasion, we put to you, you talked to Sreten Milosevic and not to Dragan Jokic, because Sreten Milosevic was at the brigade headquarters at the time. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with Sreten Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are testifying under oath. Are you sure today that you talked to Dragan Jokic and not to Sreten Milosevic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you talk to Miladin Mijatovic. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not talk to Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the conversation with the duty officer, did you inform anyone of what you had informed the duty officer? Did you tell this to anyone from the logistics department of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again please, why did you call Lazar Ristic after that? Why did you ask him for help once again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was in a position to send a group of people, since he had contacts with the defence line in the vicinity of the Orahovac elementary school. I did not call Lazar Ristic because I knew him. Lazar Ristic was at his command at the time, but he was not the commander, and that's why I talked to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked to him because you were not sure, you did not have any promise that members from the rear of the Zvornik Brigade would be sent to help with the guarding of the detainees. Was that the reason why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have already said that no one had made any promises to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. And also because -- precisely because no one made any promises to you, you tried to obtain help from the 4th Battalion as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that neither the duty operations officer, Major Jokic, or Lazar Ristic, the deputy commander of the 4th Battalion, made any promises to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us please, that afternoon, the afternoon of the 14th, how long did Sreten Milosevic remain in Orahovac carrying out the work that you have described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he leave before or after the arrival of Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember how long Milenko Jovanovic stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when this group from the logistics department of the Zvornik Brigade left Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present while they were providing security or standing guard around the gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it physically possible for you to see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the arrival of the group that had been sent by Lazar Ristic, was it necessary for them to remain there, or was it possible for them to go back to their previous engagements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not make such assessments. I did not have anything to do with saying who would stay and who could go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did this? Who made those assessments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those who arrived joined in. No one sent back anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must admit that I did not fully understand. What do you mean when you say that "no one sent back anyone"? Who was in charge of those people providing security and who was in charge of these detainees, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to say was that nobody at any point in time said: You should go back. You're no longer needed here. And I was present there throughout that time in Orahovac and was involved in the security. I provided security. But let me just add that the men who arrived at one point in time were not assigned to the area around the gym; they were assigned to the area near the fence in front of the playground, around the playground, and to the area on the opposite side to the other part of the fencing which exists on the other side as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let me -- just one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, Your Honour, and I will finish with this topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you can just tell us what the distance was from the gym, that is, between the gym and between the area where these men stood guard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were groups of people who were stationed outside the entrance to the Orahovac school gym and near the gym as well, around the gym as well. The remainder of the people were deployed alongside the fence, separating the playground from the plateau. I cannot recall whether this fencing was made of iron or not. So the distance between the gym and the fence, or rather, the road going there could be 50 metres, approximately, 100 metres at a maximum. I cannot be precise. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. This would be a convenient moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think we'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to be excused from this session, Your Honour, so I can meet with the Registrar regarding some administrative matters which are rather urgent, if that is permissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that's your own choice. On the part of the Bench, we have no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I think, you know, before you are going, would you please indicate are there any documents you are going to tender through this witness so that we do not forget you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would now like to ask you to bear with me and to continue. Analysing your statement of the 21st of January, 2004, I see that on page 4 you say what you repeated yesterday during your testimony that Drago Nikolic determined the locations for the execution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that he determined the location where the mass graves would be dug?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say about the grave locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me quote from your words that: "The engineer unit that carried out the digging, received their instructions from him," meaning Drago Nikolic. Am I quoting your words correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic told me that the engineer unit had received their tasks and that we here would have to start carrying out the preparations for the execution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try and quote your words to you again, just to see whether you still maintain it. So when asked by Mr. McCloskey how you know that Drago went and picked that location for the execution, you answer: "Well, on the basis of the digging, the engineer unit did the digging and they received their instructions from him." Is this what you have just said earlier -- I mean, six days ago. Whether -- is it correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago went to the site where this was being done; I, however, did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirmed this on page 46 of your testimony the day yesterday, and I want to elicit the following answer from you: I am fully aware of the fact that you say you were not present at the execution site. Is it correct that the engineer unit carried out the digging and that they had received their instructions from Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The engineer unit did the digging; however, I said that if Drago was there -- I don't know where they got their instructions, but probably it was from Drago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You base that on the fact that Drago was up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the engineer unit received its task to do the digging, I was not present when the arrangements were made as to when, where, and so on, they would do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also confirmed that you did not see any machinery used by engineers at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In light of what you have confirmed for us today, that the engineer unit had received its instructions from Drago Nikolic, am I correct in concluding that Drago Nikolic in Orahovac at the execution site was in charge of the machinery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present to be able to say whether Drago Nikolic was in charge of the machinery or who was in charge of the machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Drago Nikolic up there where the machinery was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic was at the site where the executions of the captured Muslims who had been accommodated in the gym of the elementary school in Orahovac were carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about one or two sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that there were two sites when you were not present at either of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that on the basis of what I knew that evening, but I know on the basis of the tasks that I had been given in this respect later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any other officer was present up there at the execution site in addition to Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now want to ask you once again: Can you confirm whether you did personally take part in the use of the machinery on the 14th of July in the afternoon hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the use of the ULT-220 machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still maintain that you did not see any kind of construction equipment or machinery there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to clarify things, you did not see any piece of construction machinery there; please confirm that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any kind of construction machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to tell me where you spent the evening of the 14th of July, where were you physically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the gym itself on the plateau in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the morning. I can't be specific about the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave that place at any point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend the night between the 14th and the 15th there at that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that you spent the night between the 14th and the 15th of July in the Zvornik Brigade command asleep in the room of the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please try to remember. Is it possible that you mistook the nights between the 14th and the 15th and between the 15th and the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not confuse the two nights.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're absolutely sure about what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the usher to assist us to show the witness the exhibit marked for identification purposes as D69.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify. This is -- already has a Prosecution marking of 399, and it may be simpler to keep it marked as what it's been marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think at this moment we'll just keep the original number there, and we'll introduce this document into the evidence. In the future if in case we could discuss whether it has a double number there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is the exhibit that we received from Mr. Butler, and the -- its designation is P399. This is the record of the presence of the attendance of the personnel of the Zvornik Brigade for July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that the little cross or little plus sign indicates that the person in question was present in the Zvornik Brigade command and that the absence of a person is indicated with a different marking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the attendance regards, you were in the Zvornik Brigade command, both on the 14th and on the 15th of July, 1995, because we have this plus sign here. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet, today under oath you claim that you were not in the Zvornik Brigade command, neither on the 14th of July in the morning, and you also say that you did not spend the night between the 14th and the 15th there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the attendance record for the officers from the Zvornik Brigade command in their units or indicating that they were carrying out the tasks they had been assigned for these specific days, which would mean -- I mean, the plus sign indicates not that I was present at the Zvornik Brigade command, but at the site where I was assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for assistance -- in order to assist you, the English translation does not have the markings, but if you refer to the B/C/S original, you will be able to see the markings there and follow the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, am I correct when I say that the letter "T" indicates that the person in question was on a field mission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me when I say that going to Orahovac would mean going on a field mission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that even those who were in the field outside of the premises of the Zvornik Brigade command had the plus sign next to their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who were in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade in the course of the day were marked with a plus sign. And all those who went to carry out missions outside of the zone of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, they would spend five or ten or even more days than that, were marked with the letter "T." This is what I assume. I don't know who kept the records in the unit and I don't know how the record was kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you see, this is precisely why we wanted to confront you with this piece of evidence. Please have a look at Item 29. Here we have the deputy commander of the brigade, Dragan Obrenovic. He testified here and he said that on that day he had not been at the Zvornik Brigade command, and in order to prove that, he had the letter "T" next to his name. And the reasoning was that he was in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, he was in command of the Zvornik Brigade at that time, and that he was at Perunika at that time. Yet, here you say something else, you say that this is not correct. That the letter "T" would be put beside somebody's name, only if that person was outside of the zone of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. Now, Witness, I want to know: Who is telling the truth? What is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who kept the record and I don't know on what basis he did that, how he recorded the attendance of all the officers in the Zvornik Brigade command, whether he put the plus signs only as a formality or whether he really checked what the situation was. The only thing that I know is that I was not at the Zvornik Brigade at that time; I was in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't want to contradict you. We only want to say that you were in the Zvornik Brigade command on the 14th and that you spent the night between the 14th and the 15th in the Zvornik Brigade command. Can this document serve to remind you and perhaps to show you that you have made a mistake as regards the dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the person keeping the record did not do that properly when he marked the attendance or that something is wrong here, that the records were not consistent. Your statement, Obrenovic's statement, or this document, it is impossible for all three to be correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to make an evaluation of the way in which the records were kept. I just wanted to say what I have just said regarding my presence there or absence there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Will you agree with me that Obrenovic is marked with the letter "T" for the dates of the 14th and the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it can be either a "T" or a plus sign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it can hardly be a plus sign, because you can see here two, three, four, five markings with -- for the letter "T" for the period of the 14th and the 17th, but we'll leave that for the consideration of the Trial Chamber. I will not be bothering you with this topic anymore. Fine. So according to your testimony, on the 15th of July in the morning, you were in the Zvornik Brigade command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time were you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 8.00 and 9.00 -- perhaps until 10.00, but that would be the latest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there the usual line-up of the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present for the line-up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it customary to have a line-up of the command personnel in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A daily line-up was customary; however, I don't know whether it indeed took place on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it because you think you arrived late or later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that the line-up always took place before 8.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw Jokic that morning, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your statement, you stayed at the command, at the headquarters, until 10.00 or thereabouts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the precise time, but I know that I stayed there only briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the permission to go home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Drago Nikolic and Popovic, did you see any other officer from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the headquarters, at the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not with Drago Nikolic or Popovic at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't meet them at any point in time outside the Zvornik Brigade headquarters on the 15th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other officer of the Zvornik Brigade in the morning of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us then what you did between 8.00 and 10.00 at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went into the office, then I went to the toilet. I don't know whether I spent there a couple of minutes or so. Then I left the headquarters, and I looked for a vehicle to transport me to Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us you didn't have any contact whatsoever, that is, with any of the officers of the Zvornik Brigade at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Sreten Milosevic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Nenad Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Ljubo Bojanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible, Witness, for you to have been present there for two hours, that is, during the most intense part of the day, not to see anyone, not to talk with anyone about what you had done, where you had been the previous night? Is it possible that you did not have any conversation whatsoever that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had finished my work at the office, I left the building and I hitchhiked. I was trying to find a lift for Kozluk, because I didn't spend two hours communicating, talking, to the officers at the brigade headquarters. However, I did say that I stayed at the headquarters no longer than two hours in total. That would have been the maximum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time did you go to Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the same period did you ever go to Pilica, and is it possible that someone saw you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Try to remember. I'm talking about the morning of the 15th. Did you go to Pilica? You are under an oath, sir. Were you there or not at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Our job will be to find out to what extent you're telling the truth today. Now, let me ask you a couple of things concerning the issue of reburial. Can you tell us when this reburial operation actually started.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the precise time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us as to the time framework when it started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in October, maybe late September, October, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this operation last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the area of Zvornik only?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the area of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about 15 days. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think it was in the latter half of September and the first half of October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again I cannot be precise as far as the time is concerned, but it would have been at that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the Zvornik Brigade headquarters was abreast of the overall operation of reburial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you clarify the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day before yesterday you testified, and I can quote the statement that you gave on the 21st and the 25th to the Prosecutor. In this regard you said that the command of the Zvornik Brigade was informed of the overall operation of reburial at all times.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were informed of the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they were abreast of, or familiar with the operation, what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were aware of the fact that it was necessary to have a reburial operation, that the primary graves had to be transferred to secondary locations, that the existing graves had to be relocated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the Zvornik Brigade, was it possible for you to carry out the work that you had received without the knowledge and the consent of the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not possible for me. I could not work without an order issued by my superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you this order? Which superior officer did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the relocation of mass graves - and this is what I stated two days ago - my first such contact, or the first information to that effect that I received was from Drago Nikolic. This was a rather unofficial contact, because he simply said that there was a possibility or that it would have necessary maybe for those mass graves to be relocated to other places. Later, I was in contact with Drago Nikolic and Popovic, the chief security officer of the Drina Corps, in the office of the security chief when this was explicitly said to me. And as I have already indicated, both of them had arrived from the office where the commander usually sat, but I don't know exactly whom they had seen before that or what kind of arrangement were agreement had been reached in this regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that the logistics of the Zvornik Brigade was also involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that assistance had been provided, that is, that two members of the logistics department had been sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding the participation of these two soldiers from the logistics department of the Zvornik Brigade, you didn't mention anything about that on the 21st and the 25th in your statement to the Prosecutor, but you did speak about it on the 19th. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. What was the first date that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have the transcript of your interview of the 19th of August, 2002, in which you spoke about the fact that members of the logistics department of the Zvornik Brigade had taken part in this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You confirmed this today, but you did not speak about it on the 21st and the 25th when you had another interview with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason being, I assume, because they did not ask you about the participation of the logistics department in this operation, so that's why you failed to mention this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reason was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that any engagement of the logistics department in an activity of this kind cannot be done without an order of the brigade commander and that no one can take part in an activity of this type on their own. Or would it have been possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who issued orders with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible for logistics department soldiers to take part in this activity without the knowledge and without a relevant order of their commander? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they cannot. It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume we know that much about military affairs. Is it possible for members of the engineer force to be part of this activity without the knowledge of their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, do not ask me about this and about such orders. I have never been a brigade commander or a brigade -- or a battalion commander. And I told you right away that I didn't know who issued orders to whom. All I know about is the tasks and the duties that I had received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a reserve captain. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have military education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a unit, such as -- can a unit be used without a relevant order for -- from the commander, and I'm talking about the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. I don't know why you were afraid to give me this answer. Who was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he present there at that time, or was he at a training by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was present there after the completion of the operations. Whether he was present at the very beginning of the operation, I don't know. Drago Nikolic would know this, as well as Popovic, the chief of security of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the engineer company at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't who the engineer commander was. I know that the chief of staff of the engineer company was Major Jokic. As to the commanders of engineer companies, I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness, there is no chief of staff of the engineer company as such. Such a function does not exist. There is only one engineer company; it has its commander. The company consisted of three platoons. We cannot talk about different company commanders. As for the name you mentioned, Dragan Jokic, he was the chief of engineer force of the Zvornik Brigade; this is just for your information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask the assistance of the usher at this point, please. I would like to elicit a comment on a document which we have identified as D67. This is a document which was introduced through Witness Butler, the reference being P541. I think we can also use this document for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, this document that we now have in front of us is the document that you were able to see yesterday at the beginning of the hearing. We mentioned the name yesterday, but let us not mention it again today, because of your situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe it would be more convenient and more comfortable for all of us if we dealt with this matter in a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you expressed a dilemma a while ago. Did you provide the Steier trucks for the transportation of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the name of the vehicles is, what is the make. I simply stated the exact reasons. But there was a vehicle - perhaps two. I'm not sure. I don't know about that - that was given by a haulier, a hauling company. Now, whether the engineer machine was malfunctioning, whether it had broken down, or whether Lazarevic had asked for another machine as backup because of the distance of Branjevo, I cannot be quite specific about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself request additional trucks to be used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, I cannot remember whether it was myself or Lazarevic, but one of us did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you determine the location for any of the secondary grave sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in contact at all about the location of the new grave sites, and I was not consulted about that. All those activities were carried out by Lazarevic from the engineer company, together with members of the 5th Engineer Battalion, in cooperation with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was whether you yourself determined the location of the secondary grave sites.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the completion of this activity, is it correct that you yourself handed in the report indicating that the operation was completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report was drafted in the office of the security chief, Drago Nikolic, and myself. This report was submitted to Popovic, the security chief of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you begin with this activity before the first quantities of fuel arrived, and did you then use the fuel from the logistics centre of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you did not use the fuel of the logistics of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not use that fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later when you received the five tonnes of fuel, you did not return the fuel that you had used before that from the Zvornik Brigade logistics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us in some detail how come that the commander of the brigade rewarded you as participants in this activity with days off and quantities of washing powder. You said that this was your proposal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not rewarded in this manner after the completion of the operation. The brigade commander, Vinko Pandurevic, was personally informed of it in his office. I told him that the participants in the operation had carried out their task at night and that as such they are entitled to days off. He said that they would be given days off and that he would relay this to the unit commanders so that I didn't have anything to do with that. And it was also said at the time, regarding the washing powder, because of the work conditions, he had spoken to Milosevic before that and asked whether there were any quantities of washing powder to be distributed among the men, and Milosevic did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the commander did both on your proposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did propose that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for all intents and purposes, you were the person in charge of the coordination of this whole activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was tasked to coordinate this group and to provide it with any assistance it may need on behalf of the Zvornik Brigade. I was tasked by the security chief of the Zvornik Brigade, Drago Nikolic, and the security chief of the Drina Corps, Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this would be a good place to stop. I have just one more set of questions, and then I will be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have several questions left, and then we will wind up. You said you had lived at one point during the war in Kozluk with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you had arrived in Kozluk in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that you had not been able to find accommodation there, so you decided to continue, to go from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I was not able to find a house, but that I could not settle down. So I wanted to solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay there for a while in June and July looking for accommodation, I mean in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spent the entire period of time in question in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you live in Kozluk? Where were you accommodated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first accommodation was on the dirt road, not far from the river. We only had one room -- there was only one room in that house, and there was no glass on the windows of that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly at this point, but -- I mean I don't know how much later, but I was -- I moved to a house and I occupied one half of a house which is located in the vicinity of the Zvornik/Kozluk road -- not far from the road, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain there until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose house was it, the one you lived in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a Serb or a Muslim house?
